January 21,

Dear Colonel,

The China Publishing Co. Inc. which owns
the "China Courier" went into liquidation on January 19.
The U. S. Court for China is appointing liquidators.
Creditors of the Co. estimate a payment of about 5, when
liquidation is completed. The printing plant reverts to
38dv.8d.VII the Linotype Co. by virtue of an agreement, the goodwill
of the Co. is practically nil and there is very little
stock-in-trade to realise upon. R. Chaney an American
citizen, who last edited the "Courier" is now employed
by the H.J.D. News Ltd.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 27, 1927

THE RED AGENTS AT LARGE
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."
SIR,—I note in your paper of to-day's date a letter signed by one "N.N.," referring to "the grip of Borodin's Red gang upon China." This letter includes a list "of the Red agents who... have travelled on British boats alone......during May and June of this year." To my amazement, I find my own name included on this list, as follows:
"26. Howard (late Courier), gone to Hankow to work with Borodin."
There is an additional statement to the effect that "these 62 worthies" (which includes myself) "are all Soviet citizens, though not all of Russian birth."
I would be pleased to have the courtesy of your columns to point out that these statements, as far as I myself am concerned, are absolute, unqualified, malicious lies. I am not a "Red agent," (which apparently means a Bolshevik propagandist or employee of some kind), am not a Soviet citizen, and have never been in Russia. There is no doubt, however, that I am the person referred to above, the reference to the "Courier" making this clear.
While this contemptible method of attack, by an individual who is apparently afraid to sign his own name, calls for no response further than an absolute denial, I feel it is only fair to you and your reading public to add a few details about myself. I am an American of Revolutionary ancestry on both sides, my mother being a member of the Daughters of Liberty, my father from the Howards of Virginia. I have now been in the Far East more than ten years, engaged in both newspaper work and commercial offices in Japan and China. In addition to my other work I have contributed to such publications as the New York "Nation," and written a number of historical and social studies some of which were collected in book form and published by the "Japan Chronicle," the British liberal paper of Kobe, Japan. In all my rather voluminous writings, whether in Japan or here, there is not to be found the slightest advocacy of Bolshevism in any way. I have never favoured the doctrine, never believed in it, and have repeatedly criticized both its theory and practice. As a liberal, I have in past years favoured the recognition of the Soviet Government by other states. I have believed them to be as much entitled to recognition as the old Tsarist government, no more and no less. Every argument regarding terrorism and outrage which can be brought against the

Soviet Government applies, in greater or lesser measure, to the old régime.
I have never advocated Bolshevism and never believed in it. In all my work, whether on the "Shanghai Times," the "China Press," the "Sporting News," or the "China Courier," there has never been anything which in any way could be construed as an advocacy of Bolshevism. During the brief period, at the time of Mr. Zia's imprisonment, when I was editor-in-chief of the "China Courier," I made my position absolutely clear and definite. Two months before the split between the Nanking and Wuhan governments on the question of Communism, I pointed out that the Communists had no place in the Kuomintang, that they did not and could not believe in the Three Peoples' Principles, that national independence, political democracy, and devotion to the people's livelihood were all equally far from their beliefs. Among the scores of editorial articles I wrote for the "China Courier," I challenge anyone to find any article which in any way, manner, shape, or form supports Bolshevik ideas.
My opposition to Bolshevism has not been profitable to me. I have more than once been offered lucrative positions by Soviet agents, but have at all times refused to engage in any work which would involve advocacy or support of Bolshevism—this in spite of the fact that I have been in very serious economic straits recently. Under the circumstances, including me in a list of well-paid Bolshevik agents is adding insult to injury.
I went to Hankow last month to gather material, as a journalist, on conditions up there, preferring personal observation to the highly coloured reports (from both sides) which had been reaching Shanghai. I was met with distinct hostility by the Proehme's, who are running the Borodin-Chen "Nationalist News Agency" and "People's Tribune." Borodin himself, probably knowing through his secretary Vilde of my attitude and ideas, refused to see me, being always "in conference," though in point of fact meeting other journalists at the same time. Mrs. Sun and other important figures I found similarly inaccessible. So much for the remark of your ingenious correspondent that I "went to Hankow to work for Borodin."
I have no desire to start a discussion on the political ideas I have expressed. I simply set them forth in justice to myself and to your readers, that there may be no misunderstanding. I have never written or said anything, at any time, which conflicts in any way with these fundamental ideas which I hold to, as expressed above. I am a liberal, critical of certain phases of Imperialism (Soviet imperialism as well as other imperialisms), and not a Bolshevik. And I am a poor man to day because of my attitude.
I am, etc.,
HARRY PAXTON HOWARD.
Shanghai, July 26, 1927.

在逃的红色特工
致《字林西报》编辑：
先生，——我在贵报今日刊登的信件中注意到，一位署名“N.N.”的人提到了“鲍罗廷红色团伙对中国的控制”。该信包含一份“仅乘坐英国船只……在今年五月和六月期间旅行的红色特工名单”。令我惊讶的是，我发现自己的名字也列在其中，如下所示：
“26. Howard（前《信使报》人员），已去汉口为鲍罗廷工作。”
此外还有声明称，“这62位贤达”（包括我本人在内）“均为苏联公民，尽管并非全部出生于俄罗斯。”
我很希望能借助贵报版面指出，就我个人而言，这些陈述是绝对的、毫无保留的、恶意的谎言。我不是“红色特工”（这显然意味着布尔什维克宣传员或某种雇员），不是苏联公民，也从未去过俄罗斯。不过，毫无疑问，上文所指的就是我本人，提及《信使报》(Courier) 使这一点变得明确。
虽然这种由一个显然不敢署真名的人采用的卑鄙攻击手段，除了绝对否认外无需其他回应，但我觉得为了对贵报及读者公平起见，补充一些关于我个人的细节是恰当的。我是美国人，父母双方均有革命血统，母亲是自由之女社 (Daughters of Liberty) 成员，父亲来自弗吉尼亚州的霍华德家族 (Howards of Virginia)。我在远东已逾十年，在日本和中国的报社及商业机构任职。除其他工作外，我还向纽约《民族》周刊 (Nation) 等刊物投稿，并撰写了许多历史和社会研究文章，其中一些被汇编成书，由日本神户的英国自由派报纸《日本纪事报》(Japan Chronicle) 出版。在我相当大量的著作中，无论在日本还是在此地，都找不到丝毫以任何方式倡导布尔什维主义的内容。我从未赞成该学说，从未相信过它，并多次批评其理论和实践。作为一名自由主义者，我在过去几年曾主张其他国家承认苏维埃政府。我认为他们与旧的沙皇政府一样有权获得承认，不多也不少。任何针对

苏维埃政府的恐怖主义和暴行指控，在更大或更小程度上也适用于旧政权。
我从未倡导过布尔什维主义，也从未相信过它。在我的所有工作中，无论是在《上海泰晤士报》(Shanghai Times)、《密勒氏评论报》(China Press)、《体育新闻》(Sporting News) 还是《中国信使报》(China Courier)，没有任何内容可以被解释为倡导布尔什维主义。在夏志方 (Mr. Zia) 入狱期间，我担任《中国信使报》主编的短暂时期内，我的立场非常清晰和明确。在南京和武汉政府就共产主义问题分裂前的两个月，我就指出共产党人在国民党内没有位置，他们并不且不可能相信三民主义，民族独立、政治民主和对民生福祉的热忱都与他们的信念相去甚远。在我为《中国信使报》撰写的数十篇社论文章中，我挑战任何人找出任何以任何方式、形式支持布尔什维克思想的文章。
我对布尔什维主义的反对并未给我带来利益。苏联特工曾多次向我提供高薪职位，但我始终拒绝从事任何涉及倡导或支持布尔什维主义的工作——尽管我最近经济状况非常困难。在这种情况下，将我列入高薪布尔什维克特工名单简直是雪上加霜。
上个月我去汉口，以记者身份收集当地情况的材料，比起传至上海的各方色彩浓烈的报道，我更倾向于亲身观察。我遭到了普罗梅夫妇 (Proehme's) 的明显敌视，他们经营着鲍罗廷-陈氏“国民党新闻社”和《人民论坛报》。鲍罗廷本人，可能通过其秘书维尔德 (Vilde) 知晓我的态度和想法，拒绝见我，总是“在开会”，尽管事实上他当时正在会见其他记者。我发现孙夫人和其他重要人物同样难以接近。这就反驳了贵报那位高明通讯员说我“去汉口为鲍罗廷工作”的说法。
我不希望就开始讨论我所表达的政治观点。我只是为了对自己和读者公正而陈述这些观点，以免产生误解。在任何时候，我都未曾写过或说过任何与我上述坚持的基本理念相冲突的内容。我是一名自由主义者，批判帝国主义的某些方面（包括苏维埃帝国主义以及其他帝国主义），而不是布尔什维克。而且，因为我的态度，我今天是个穷人。
此致，
敬礼
HARRY PAXTON HOWARD.
上海，1927年7月26日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, JULY 26, 1927

THE RED AGENTS AT LARGE
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."
SIR,—Readers of all nationalities have read with interest and satisfaction the series of articles which you are publishing about the grip of Borodin's Red gang upon China. Some of us know that it is all true and a great deal besides. Others in official positions ought to know it all if they do not. But every-one must be wondering, as I often have, why so little is done. Why is so little being done even now when you and your public know so much. There is one of Borodin's sayings that is most quoted in the Russian communities in China, which is to this effect: "While the British are talking we are acting." You have given us a great deal more to talk about now, but you give us very little news of any action yet except Borodin's. As your contributor knows and reveals, and as Chiang Kai-shek's subordinates know, as your police know or should, nearly every British boat that goes up and down the coast or up and down the Yangtze River, carries active agents of the Soviet, working by fair or foul means against British and all other foreign interests. The names they give are not always their own, but even their aliases are often associated with enough crime to hang a dozen times over. They come here and use this Settlement and work against its peace. But no check is put upon them, though they seldom move without contraband. Just to show that I know what I am writing about I shall give here a list of the Red agents who, to own knowledge, have travelled on British boats alone, in and out of this harbour, during May and June of this year. As many again travelled on boats of other nationalities.
Here they are:
1. Pohvalinsky, arrived from Vladivostok, has gone to Hankow, returned to Shanghai under the name Berdis and is nominated as Consul in Canton.
2. Vilde, arrived in May from Moscow and under the name of Roubinchik has gone to Hankow.
3. Rasolnikoff, alias Ilyn, arrived in May and under the name of Tessman has left for Hankow.
4. Oukoloff, from the Moscow State Political Government, arrived here in May and June and has since left.
5. Dablin, propagandist and agitator arrived in Canton in may returned Shanghai and left for Hankow.
6. Zvetkoff, left for Hankow in June, returned and left for Vladivostok.
7. Shenisheff, arrived from Hankow and left for Vladivostok.
8. Moussin, Comintern Agent, arrived here from Bulgaria and left for Hankow, is possessor of a card of "Tass" Agent.
9. Grishin, ("Tass") went to Canton, returned in June and again left for Hankow.
10. de Sheimo, stayed in Hongkong and Canton, returned to Shanghai.
11. Simini, Comintern Agent, "Minister of Labour", arrived here from Hankow and left for Vladivostock.
11A. Kalachioff, Borodin's "head of department of unions" arrived here and left for Moscow.
12. Nikitin, Red Military Officer, went through Shanghai in June and left for Canton.
13. Roudneff, ex-G.H.Q. General, arrived here from Tientsin and left for Hankow.
14. Radkevich, military engineer, arrived from Moscow and left for Hankow.
15. Zotoff, has visited Shanghai many times from Nanking; and was recently back in Nanking; adviser to the Nationalist Government.
16. Koslovsky, went in June to Hankow and is now back.
17. Peticff, leader of Cheka in Hankow, came here and left twice in May.
18. Ostrovsky, came to Shanghai from Tientsin in June.
19. Kouznetsoff, coding clerk, went through here in June.
20. Borovoy, ex-secretary of Mukden Consulate, deported by Chang Tso-lin from China, went to Hankow, came back and left for Vladivostok.
21. Bogroff, went from Hankow to Vladivostok via Shanghai.
22. Amber, arrived here from Tientsin to purchase medical supplies for Feng's Army and ammunition for forces stationed in Mongolia, has gone back.
23. Novichenkoff, has gone to Vladivostok.
24. Dobrijsher, agent of Comintern, with a "Tass" card, went to Hankow.
25. Weber, Military Agent, gone to Hankow, came here from Canton.
26. Howard, (Late Courier) gone to Hankow to work with Borodin.
27. Fingelskold, gone to Swatow, co-worker and assistant of Zaproudsky who used to be president of the Cheka at Irkoutsk.

55. Iolk, adviser on agrarian affairs, arrived from Hankow.

It will be noted by those familiar with the Red organization that these 62 worthies are all Soviet citizens, though not all of Russian birth. The list could be greatly lengthened by the inclusion of Communists of other nationalities, co-operating in China with Borodin's Soviet agents. Among these I think most of us are now familiar with at least one or more American, British, Japanese, German, Austrian, Hungarian and other citizens or subjects. These persons travel as much and as freely as the Soviet citizens. A very little check on the movements of passenger on river and coastwise steamers by a passably intelligent secret service would enable the Municipal authorities to mark every one of these persons that entered this port and, through co-operation with the Chinese, to put such restrictions on their movements as would seriously circumscribe Borodin's activities. It really does not seem amusing to me that foreign gunboats in the river and the ports should be guaranteeing safe passage to Bolsheviks whose sole business is to promote a virulent anti-foreign campaign, nor that this Settlement should be made a distributing centre for anti-foreign literature and other contraband that travels with these agents in foreign steamers.
I am, etc.,
N. N.
Shanghai, July 23, 1927.

赤色代理人逍遥法外

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生——各国籍的读者都饶有兴致且满意地阅读了贵报正在连载的关于鲍罗廷（Borodin）的赤色团伙如何控制中国的系列文章。我们中的一些人知道，这些报道不仅全部属实，而且揭露的内容远不止于此。其他身居官位的人如果尚不知情，理应知晓这一切。但每个人一定都在纳闷，正如我常有的疑问那样，为何采取的行动如此寥寥。既然您和公众已经知晓如此之多，为何即便在此时，采取的行动依然如此之少？在中国俄国人社区中，鲍罗廷有一句被引用最多的名言，大意是：“当英国人在空谈时，我们在行动。”如今，您给了我们更多谈论的材料，但除了鲍罗廷的行动外，您几乎没有提供任何关于采取实际行动的消息。正如您的撰稿人所知并披露的那样，也如蒋介石的下属所知，以及您的警察所知或应知的那样，几乎每一艘往返于沿海或长江上下航行的英国船只，都载有苏联的活跃代理人，他们通过正当或不正当手段，损害英国及所有其他外国利益。他们使用的名字并不总是真名，但即使是他们的化名，所关联的罪行也足以让他们被绞死十几次。他们来到这里，利用本租界，破坏其和平。然而，尽管他们鲜有不携带违禁品行动的情况，却未受到任何遏制。为了表明我对所写内容确有所知，我将在此列出一份赤色代理人名单。据我所知，仅在今年五月和六月期间，这些人就单独乘坐英国船只进出本港。还有同样多的人乘坐其他国籍的船只旅行。

名单如下：

1. 波哈林斯基（Pohvalinsky），从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达，已前往汉口，以伯迪斯（Berdis）之名返回上海，并被提名为驻广州领事。

此致，
N. N.
上海，1927年7月23日。

the management of the newspaper or any member of the Foreign
Staff. Both Messrs Davey and Mayer state that they will
instruct their staff not to print the China Courier again.

THE CHINA COURIER, WEDNESDAY, JULY 6, 1927

$1,000 PRIZE CONTEST

THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS WILL GOVERN

(1) The questionnaire which appears below must be answered in full.
(2) Answers must reach THE CHINA COURIER on or before October 31st, 1927.
(3) All answers must be sent to the Editor, $1,000 Prize Contest, China Courier.

The judges for this contest will be composed of three prominent Shanghai residents, viz; the president of a local law school, a practising Chinese lawyer and the editor of the China Courier.

A

1.—Does a state of war exist, when one nation
(a) bombards a city or a port of another or
(b) lands and stations armed forces on the territory of another without the consent and against the will, and manifestly for the purpose of waging war with, that other?
2.—Can one belligerent nation bombard an undefended city or port of another with which the former is at war?
3.—When a state of war exists between two nations,
(a) what is the position of their treaties?
(b) can the subjects of those nations have contractual or social relations with one another?
4.—When the person or property of the citizens of a friendly nation is injured or destroyed in a riot or war taking place in the territory of another nation,
(a) is the government of the latter nation liable for compensation, and/or
(b) can the government of the former nation land and/or station armed forces in the territory of the latter to protect such person or property without creating a state of war between those two nations?
5.—Under what circumstances, is the government of one nation justified to call upon that of another to recall its diplomatic or consular agent?

B

1.—Under what treaty provisions and which land regulation or regulations does the Shanghai Municipal Council derive its authority to secure land in Shanghai for the purposes of (a) road construction and (b) public recreation?
2.—How far and in what way or ways is such authority limited?
3.—For what purpose or purposes are the Municipal roads and recreation grounds to be used?
4.—If the Shanghai Municipal Council allows a foreign government to use the Municipal roads and grounds for the armed forces of that government without the consent and against the will of the Chinese Government, or for a purpose hostile to China, what is the legal position of:—
(a) the Council and
(b) the roads and grounds so used?

C

1.—What is a foreigner's right to hold land in China based on treaty provisions?
2.—What is the nature and process of tenure of holding in land at Shanghai under a Consular Title Deed?
3.—Apart from trade and residence, can a foreign holder of land at Shanghai use the land for any other purpose or purposes?
4.—Can he let any of the following Governments station armed forces on the land and construct fortifications thereon:—
(a) Chinese government?
(b) his own government?
(c) any other government?
5.—If may, is the land liable to forfeiture?

D

1.—What are the historical connections and significance of the following expressions and who uttered them and what is your opinion thereon?
(a) "a scrap of paper."
(b) "necessity knows no Law."
(c) "Right of necessity."
2.—How far is self protection a justifiable plea in Law?

1,000美元奖金竞赛

以下条款将作为准则

(1) 必须完整回答下列问卷。
(2) 答案必须在1927年10月31日或之前送达《中国信使报》。
(3) 所有答案必须寄给编辑，注明“1,000美元奖金竞赛”，《中国信使报》。

本次竞赛的评委将由三位上海知名人士组成，即：一所本地法学院的院长、一位执业中国律师以及《中国信使报》的编辑。

(b) 其本国政府？
(c) 任何其他政府？
5.—如果可以，该土地是否面临被没收的风险？

H-2. HOWARD, Harry, F.
An American citizen, born in Camden, New Jersey in 1893, with pronounced Communist sympathies. Went to Russia in 1917, and arrived in Shanghai July 29, 1922 from Japan.
First employed with Asia Life Insurance Co., but later joined staff of reporters on the "Shanghai Times". Owing to his extreme radical views he lost his position and joined the staff of the "China Press" newspaper. He stayed with this paper for 2 years but attempted to introduce Communistic doctrines into his articles and did not hesitate to express verbally his sympathies with the Communist movement and was known to frequent the local U.S.S.R. Consulate.
Howard then edited a small weekly newspaper called the "Sports and Amusements Weekly", but failed financially. He then joined the staff of the "China Courier" as Editor with L. Klindt Kentwell, but recently left this employment and is reported to have now left Shanghai.
Howard has been engaged in journalistic work practically all his life, and during a visit to Japan published a book entitled "The Socialist and Labour Movement in Japan" published in Kobe in 1921. He did not register as an American citizen in Shanghai until July 30th. 1925.

H-2. 霍华德（HOWARD），哈里（Harry），F.
美国公民，1893年出生于新泽西州卡姆登，具有明显的共产主义同情倾向。1917年前往俄国，并于1922年7月29日从日本抵达上海。
最初受雇于亚洲人寿保险公司（Asia Life Insurance Co.），但后来加入《上海泰晤士报》记者团队。由于其极端的激进观点，他失去了职位，并加入了《字林西报》报社。他在该报工作了2年，但试图在其文章中引入共产主义教义，并毫不掩饰地口头表达其对共产主义运动的同情，众所周知他经常出入当地苏联领事馆。
霍华德随后编辑了一份名为《体育与娱乐周刊》的小型周报，但在财务上失败。此后，他与 L. 克林特·肯特韦尔（L. Klindt Kentwell）一起加入《中国信使报》担任编辑，但最近已离职，据报现已离开上海。
霍华德几乎一生都从事新闻工作，在访问日本期间，于1921年在神户出版了一本名为《日本的社会主义与劳工运动》的书。直到1925年7月30日，他才在上海登记为美国公民。

This Co. is a purely British concern and supplied the linotype machines used by the China Publishing Co. which owns and prints the "Courier".

The agreement further provides that, if monthly instalments are not promptly paid, the Linotype Co. are entitled, without warning, to seize the machinery. The China Publishing Co. are four months behind in their payments and owe the Linotype Co. an approximate sum of $3,000.

THE CHINA COURIER, TUESDAY, MAY 3, 1927.

War Scenes Shift To Devil's
Alley; Nordic Crusaders At
Odds With Latin Defenders

Despite barbed wire barricades, the center of China's war has been moved from the vicinity of Pu-tow to Rue Chu Pao San, otherwise known as the Devil's Alley, in Frenchtown.

The Chinese have nothing to do with this latest civil war excepting in the capacity of innocent bystanders. All the gore is just the result of a little friendly fight, presumably to keep in practise, between the brave defenders of western civilization who are here to give the Chinese free lessons in maintaining peace and order.

This new war, which threatens to make Nanking look like a picnic, is Latin vs. Nordic. On the Latin side are the French and Italian defenders of civilization; on the Nordic side are the British and American preservers of peace. As we go to press, the Latin is triumphant and the Nordic is down but not out.

It all began several weeks ago. Down in the Devil's Alley are various places of recreation for he-men with hair on their chests, among them being Mumm's, the Alcazar, the New Royal, and the "Gay Paree." Around the corner is O. B.'s that has long been the headquarters of American "gobs" ashore.

Here the lights were bright and life was lurid. Here blared the saxophones until far unto the dawn while graceful maids wiggled and writhed and soothed the fevered brows of bronzed crusaders from many western lands.

Alas, most of these emporiums of joy were dark last night. The saxophones were silent and the Muscovite maids were lonely of heart and short on cash. 'Twas like that famous day in Mudville when the mighty Casey struck out.

Devil's Alley had been placed out of bounds to British and American crusaders.

"Why keep open for the Frogs and the Wops?" said one cabaret manager. "They 'aint got no money to spend."

Consequently the Latin victory is like the saving of Shanghai: it don't mean anything.

Exact details of the Latin-Nordic war are still lacking and the exact number of casualties to date are not known. Several went to the hospital some days ago in a pitched battle in Devil's Alley and a skirmish took place last Saturday night which resulted in closing the cabarets at nine o'clock. Whereupon the British authorities placed the alley out of bounds for their crusaders. The French officials, it is understood, then ordered all American "gobs" to stay out of the various cabarets and the American authorities followed suit by placing Devil's Alley out of bounds.

Many of the cabarets retaliated by closing up.

"There isn't any profit in keeping open for the French and Italians," said one cabaret manager yesterday. "They come into the place, buy a bottle of beer between six of them, and dance with each other. When you tell them this is against the rules they threaten to throw you out of your own place. The British haven't got much to spend. All the profit is in the American trade."

So Devil's Alley is dark and deserted excepting for police and patrols. They are there in large numbers for it is reported that irate "gobs" are planning to make a raid on their favorite recreation grounds and thus restore Nordic prestige in Frenchtown.

战事移至“魔鬼巷”；北欧十字军与拉丁捍卫者发生冲突

尽管设有铁丝网路障，中国战事的中心已从浦东附近转移至法租界的朱葆三路（Rue Chu Pao San），即俗称的“魔鬼巷”。

中国人在这场最新的内战中除了作为无辜的旁观者外，并无任何牵涉。所有的流血事件仅仅是西方文明勇敢捍卫者之间一场小小的“友好争斗”的结果，这些人来到这里是为了给中国人免费提供维持和平与秩序的课程， presumably 是为了保持实战状态。

这场新战争有可能让南京看起来像是一次野餐，其性质是拉丁裔对北欧裔。拉丁一方是法国和意大利的文明捍卫者；北欧一方则是英国和美国的和平维护者。截至本刊付印时，拉丁一方取得胜利，北欧一方虽处下风但并未出局。

这一切始于几周前。在“魔鬼巷”里，分布着各种供胸膛长毛的硬汉们娱乐的场所，其中包括穆姆酒馆（Mumm's）、阿尔卡萨剧院（Alcazar）、新皇家剧院（New Royal）以及“快乐巴黎”（Gay Paree）。拐角处是O. B.酒吧，长期以来一直是美国上岸水兵（"gobs"）的总部。

这里灯火通明，生活光怪陆离。萨克斯风一直吹奏到黎明时分，而优雅的舞女们扭动身躯，抚慰来自许多西方国家的晒得黝黑的十字军战士那发热的额头。

唉，昨晚这些欢乐的大多数场所都漆黑一片。萨克斯风沉默了，俄罗斯舞女们内心孤独且囊中羞涩。这就像著名的马德维尔（Mudville）日子里，强大的凯西（Casey）三振出局时的情景一样。

“魔鬼巷”已被禁止英国和美国的十字军战士进入。

“为什么要为法国佬（Frogs）和意大利佬（Wops）开门营业？”一位歌舞厅经理说。“他们没钱花。”

因此，拉丁人的胜利就像拯救上海一样：毫无意义。

关于拉丁-北欧战争的确切细节仍然缺乏，确切的伤亡人数至今未知。几天前，在“魔鬼巷”的一场激战中有几人被送往医院，上周六晚发生了一场小规模冲突，导致歌舞厅在九点钟关闭。随后，英国当局禁止其十字军战士进入该巷。据悉，法国官员随后命令所有美国水兵不得进入各类歌舞厅，美国当局也效仿此举，将“魔鬼巷”列为禁地。

许多歌舞厅以关门停业作为报复。

“为法国人和意大利人开门营业无利可图，”一位歌舞厅经理昨天说。“他们走进店里，六个人合买一瓶啤酒，然后互相跳舞。当你告诉他们这违反规定时，他们威胁要把你赶出你自己的店。英国人也没多少钱可花。所有的利润都来自美国人的生意。”

因此，“魔鬼巷”除了警察和巡逻队外，一片黑暗且空无一人。那里聚集了大量警力，因为有报道称愤怒的水兵正计划突袭他们喜爱的娱乐场所，从而在法租界恢复北欧人的威望。

THE CHINA COURIER, WEDNESDAY, MAY 4, 1927.

To The 6th U. S. Marines
Welcome To Shanghai!

We welcome you as stalwart sons of whom the Great
Republic of the West is justly proud.
We welcome you because we know you are here only to
protect the lives and property of your fellow countrymen and
not for the purpose of pulling "chestnuts out of the fire"
for another power.
We welcome you because we have no fear that you will
do as the British have done and invade Chinese territory out-
side of the International Settlement.
We welcome you knowing that your views on imperialism
are the same as your forbears who twice fought and twice
vanquished British imperialism in your native land. We
welcome you because we know you are of the same mould as
your forbears who succeeded in ridding your shores of British
bayonets and British gunboats in 1776 and 1812.
We welcome you because the United States and China
are friends who have had a common foe in their struggle
against imperialism.

让英国自己从中国
火中取栗
亚瑟·布里斯班建议

“美国是否要因为英国需要维护其亚洲威望而花费更多数十亿资金、牺牲更多生命？”他问道

以下是国际知名记者亚瑟·布里斯班（Arthur Brisbane）撰写的社论，发表于4月3日的《洛杉矶考察家报》（Los Angeles Examiner）。《中国信使报》的政策通常不在主要新闻版面转载其他出版物的社论，但鉴于上海某些人士对柯立芝总统不干涉中国政策所持的态度，我们认为这篇社论对于那些倾向于认为总统政策软弱的上海居民具有特殊的兴趣。

英国将不惜一切代价维持其在中国的财产和威望，因为她必须这样做。
受英国统治的三亿亚洲人在印度注视着中国，并自问：“如果一亿亚洲人能将英国人赶出中国，为什么我们不能将他们赶出印度？”
因为她在亚洲及整个帝国的威望要求如此，英国将不惜一切代价，根据长期公认的条约，保持其在中国贸易和地方权威中的地位。如果谈判失败，英国陆军部将轰炸中国人，使用所有现代战争手段。
但是这对我们这个国家意味着什么？我们没有“必须”这样做的理由。我们在亚洲没有押注于胁迫中国能力的帝国。虽然涉及一些大型石油利益，但这些利益可以通过少于任何小型战争成本的金额收买。法国和日本向我们展示了数百万美国人应该怎么做。日本会抗议中国暴民的行为，但不会使用武力。那是没必要的，战争会威胁到这个国家商人的繁荣，这是最新的公告。法国对此持观望态度，让英国去处理中国问题，如果我们愚蠢到足以与一个不幸的、被革命和内战撕裂的国家发生严重争吵，法国甚至会在这个国家的帮助下关注中国。
在大战争中，我们为整个欧洲火中取栗，代价是在国外花费了十亿美元，在国内浪费、挥霍和贪污了五十亿美元。
我们要因为英国需要击败中国、维护其亚洲威望和印度帝国而花费更多数十亿资金、牺牲更多生命吗？
据说英国政府正敦促我国加入胁迫中国的行列，“发现我们的态度令人失望地模糊。”让我们希望我们的态度变得明确，并采取以下形式：
不，谢谢，我们不是专业的、无可救药的“火中取栗者”。
我们打算通过将本国公民撤出中国来保护他们。然后我们将把中国留给中国人，正如我们将美国留给美国人一样。如果我们的英国兄弟觉得他们必须进行一场中国战争，那是他们的事。我们既不分担也不资助。

THE CHINA COURIER. MONDAY, FEBRUARY 14, 1927.

The Question Of Language

A letter from a missionary correspondent, which we reproduce in another column, has inspired us to a certain amount of heart-searching. Sunday is traditionally a good day for thinking differently than one think during the rest of the week, and to the present writer it means a day off, in which he can meditate upon the right and wrong of the things upon which his daily journalistic duties oblige him to be prompt, quick-thinking, and incisive.

Upon due consideration, the Editor is inclined to "pipe down." Not that we have written anything wrong or misleading. Quite the contrary. Our articles and leaders have been as accurate and as fair as we could make them. The point is, however, that as one gets into the week's work, sees the glaring examples of dishonest, vindictive, and vicious journalism around one, with invention, insinuation, slander and abuse running wild, a writer feels that he is engaged in a bitter struggle in which the niceties of expression may be at times lost sight of. Not that we would ever stoop to the dishonesty and deliberate falsification characteristic of some of our "yellow" contemporaries: we certainly have never come down to this. We have, however, come down somewhat to their own language; spoken in terms which they could understand; expressed ourselves so forcibly as to create a surface reminder of some of their own journalistic methods.

This is an explanation, not an apology. It is the wish of THE CHINA COURIER to stand above the petty and puerile in journalism. Whatever our contemporaries may do or say, we hope to keep ourselves clear and clean. After all, war time and war talk, which are the things which supply an explanation for the conduct of some of our contemporaries, will pass, and in the long run (as happened a few years ago) intelligent men will forget as soon as possible the wild and vicious inventions, the scurrilous and abusive language, characteristic of a war period. In the meantime, we will try not to lapse in any way towards the level of these contemporaries even though their own provocative attitude is extremely infectious.

It is rather difficult, it is true, to maintain elegant and graceful language when opponents are indulging in the picturesque and forceful expressions characteristic of Billingsgate or the Barbary Coast. Any gentleman who has had the misfortune to get down to a really serious argument with an intoxicated stevedore will understand what we mean. However, we must remember that we are writing for the public, not for other journalists, and there is no reason why we should model our methods after, or permit them to be influenced by, any of our British contemporaries,—which unfortunately means all our morning contemporaries in the English language. After all, our mother tongue is rich enough to permit of expressing almost anything worth expressing without descending to abuse or vulgarity, and expression in good and temperate English is a worthy aim, even if it is not the present custom in Shanghai.

语言问题

一位传教士通讯员的来信（本刊另栏予以刊登）促使我们进行了一定程度的自省。星期日传统上是一个适合以不同于平日思维方式进行思考的日子，对本文作者而言，这意味着一个休息日，他可以借此沉思那些日常新闻工作职责要求他迅速反应、敏捷思考和尖锐表达的事物之是非曲直。

经过慎重考虑，本编辑倾向于“收敛锋芒”。这并非因为我们写了任何错误或误导性的内容。恰恰相反。我们的文章和社论已尽可能做到准确和公正。然而，关键在于，当一个人投入一周的工作，看到周围充斥着不诚实、报复性和恶毒的新闻报道的 glaring 例子，虚构、暗示、诽谤和谩骂肆意横行时，作家会觉得自己卷入了一场激烈的斗争，其中表达的细微之处有时会被忽视。这并不是说我们会屈尊去效仿某些“黄色”同行所特有的不诚实和故意伪造：我们当然从未堕落到这种地步。然而，我们在语言上确实向他们有所靠拢；使用他们能理解的术语；表达方式如此强烈，以至于在表面上让人联想到他们的一些新闻手法。

这是一种解释，而非道歉。《中国信使报》的愿望是超越新闻界中的琐碎和幼稚。无论我们的同行做什么或说什么，我们希望保持自身的清白和纯洁。毕竟，战时状态和战争言论——这些为某些同行的行为提供了解释的因素——终将过去，从长远来看（正如几年前发生的那样），明智的人们将尽快忘记那些狂野和恶毒的捏造，以及那些具有战争时期特征的污言秽语和辱骂性语言。与此同时，我们将努力避免在任何方面滑落到这些同行的水平，尽管他们自身的挑衅态度极具传染性。

诚然，当对手沉溺于具有比林斯盖特（Billingsgate，伦敦鱼市，以粗俗骂街闻名）或巴巴里海岸（Barbary Coast，旧金山红灯区，以混乱暴力闻名）特色的生动且有力的表达时，要保持优雅得体的语言是相当困难的。任何曾不幸与一名醉酒的码头工人进行真正严肃争论的绅士都会明白我们的意思。然而，我们必须记住，我们是写给公众看的，而不是写给其他记者看的，我们没有理由模仿我们的英国同行——不幸的是，这意味着我们在上海的所有英文晨报同行——的方法，或允许我们的方法受其影响。毕竟，我们的母语足够丰富，足以表达几乎所有值得表达的内容，而无需降格为谩骂或庸俗，用良好且适度的英语进行表达是一个值得追求的目标，即使这并非上海当前的风尚。

THE CHINA COURIER, MONDAY, FEBRUARY 14, 1927.

Are We Anti-British?

There is being circulated a canard, assiduously spread by certain dishonest persons and probably aided by a certain editorial indiscretion on our part, that THE CHINA COURIER is anti-British. This, let us state quite definitely, is not true.

The present writer, though an American, has worked for years for a British paper, writing feature articles with a very intimate bearing upon political life, and earning himself the full confidence of the owners and editors of the paper in question. He is proud to number among his friends many Englishmen, some of whom at least he can refer to as among the finest and noblest men whom he has ever known; some of them, it may be added, of very high rank in the British peerage. He is personally of Irish and Anglo-Saxon ancestry, and believes in the highest of Anglo-Saxon and American traditions: he recognizes no greater political and social ideal than the conception of tolerance and fair play, the noblest heritage of the Anglo-Saxon peoples. He regards the links of language, culture, and tradition, existing today among the children of England whose communities stretch around the globe, as things to be cherished and treasured for generations to come.

Here we have all the essentials for a 100-per-cent Anglophile. All the essentials, that is, except one: the readiness to accept as forever right and just anything the British State may consider a necessary part of their program. It was just this refusal to accept the infallibility of the British State that resulted in the United States of America coming into existence as a free and independent nation. Even in that day, however, it was not simply a struggle between Britain and the United Colonies. It was also a struggle between the Crown and some of His Majesty's loyal subjects in Parliament, where some of the best friends of the American Revolution were to be found.

Were the Parliamentary supporters of the American Revolution anti-British? It does not appear so,—not at this historical distance, anyway. On the contrary, they were the forerunners of the new Imperial policy which has resulted today in the remarkable federation of virtually sovereign states which we know as the British Commonwealth of Nations today. The old Imperial policy, in the opinion of many erudite scholars and brilliant statesmen, could have led only to the breakup of the British Empire by the splitting off of the Colonies as independent states, even as happened with the Spanish and Portuguese colonies in America. The true patriots, it appears today, the men who have held the British Empire together, were the men who were willing to abandon the old Imperial policy, who were willing to permit that development of self-government among the children of England that has finally resulted in the British Empire being transformed into a group of autonomous communities, "equal in status, in no way subordinate one to another in any aspect of their domestic or external affairs."

《中国信使报》，1927年2月14日，星期一。

我们是否反英？

目前正流传着一个谣言，由某些不诚实的人竭力散布，并可能得到了我们方面某种编辑疏忽的助长，声称《中国信使报》是反英的。让我们非常明确地声明，这不是事实。

本文作者虽是美国人，但曾为一家英国报纸工作多年，撰写与政治生活密切相关的特写文章，并赢得了该报所有者和编辑的充分信任。他自豪地将许多英国人列为朋友，其中至少有一些人可以被称为他所认识的最优秀、最高尚的人；顺便提一下，其中一些人在英国贵族阶层中拥有很高的地位。他个人具有爱尔兰和盎格鲁-撒克逊血统，并信奉盎格鲁-撒克逊和美国传统中最崇高的部分：他认为没有比宽容和公平竞赛的观念更伟大的政治和社会理想了，这是盎格鲁-撒克逊民族最高贵的遗产。他将当今遍布全球的英格兰子孙之间存在的语言、文化和传统纽带，视为值得为后代珍视和宝贵的财富。

这里具备了一个百分之百亲英派的所有要素。也就是说，除了一个要素之外：即愿意接受英国政府认为其计划中必要部分的任何事物为永远正确和公正。正是这种拒绝接受英国政府无误性的态度，导致了美利坚合众国作为一个自由独立国家的诞生。然而，即使在那时，这也不仅仅是英国与美国殖民地之间的斗争。这也是王室与议会中陛下的一些忠诚臣民之间的斗争，在美国革命中最好的一些朋友正是在那里找到的。

美国革命的议会支持者们是反英的吗？看起来并非如此——至少从这段历史距离来看并非如此。相反，他们是新帝国政策的先驱，这一政策导致了今天我们所知的英联邦（British Commonwealth of Nations）这一实际上由主权国家组成的非凡联盟。在许多博学的学者和杰出的政治家看来，旧的帝国政策只能导致大英帝国因殖民地分裂为独立国家而解体，正如美洲的西班牙和葡萄牙殖民地所发生的那样。如今看来，真正的爱国者，那些维系大英帝国团结的人，是那些愿意放弃旧帝国政策的人，是那些愿意允许英格兰子孙发展自治的人，这最终导致大英帝国转变为一组自治共同体，“地位平等，在其国内或对外事务的任何方面互不从属。”

pages.en:
But there are still survivals of the same mistaken policy
of force. It is these things that we are thoroughly and
uncompromisingly opposed to. We are opposed to them not
because they are British, but because they are out of step with
the great liberative movement of the age which we are doing
our best to support. Our opposition to the policy known as
saber-rattling applies whether the aggressor is British, Rus-
sian, or Italian, whether American, French, German, or
Japanese. We hope that China will become a free and
sovereign state. We as heartily hope that China will never
be a menace to the freedom of any other state.

We believe that the plan of the British War Office in
sending troops for the occupation of Chinese territory sur-
rounding Shanghai was a most ill-advised and provocative
one, to say nothing of the grave questions of international
law involved. We think that the failure of Reuter's agency
to send any news regarding these plans, which however
were sent out by a responsible American agency with a
correspondent in London, are evidence of an attempt (not
necessarily on the part of Reuter's Shanghai office) to keep
people of the Far East in ignorance of these plans. We think
that the spreading of a false and misleading report to the
effect that a four-power agreement had been made for the
defence of Shanghai was deliberate propaganda, wherever
it originated. We believe that these activities of the mili-
tarists and propagandists deliberately played into the hands
of the people who were and are attempting to prevent a
peaceful and equitable settlement between Britain and
China, and did much to nullify the excellent impression which
was being created by the intelligent, statesmanlike, and fair
attitude of Britain's diplomats in China recently.

It became clear a few days ago that in spite of all that
the militarists at home and the old-line Imperialists in China
could do to keep up the ancient policy of the mailed fist, the
movement of troops was being stopped, and that there would
be no more troop movements beyond Hongkong. Our con-
clusion that this was being done was confirmed by the speech
in Parliament which we gave to our readers on Saturday.
Together with this came the assurance, most important of
all, that there would be no invasion of Chinese territory, and
that the troops would remain in the Settlement. It had also
become clear that the Municipal Council of the International
Settlement, as an international governing body, was not
putting Settlement territory at the disposal of British troops,
and that such forces would have to stay on British property.

The concise phrase in which we expressed our satisfac-
tion at this defeat of jingoist policy, "Great Britain is Piping
Down," was perhaps not exactly delicate. Also, the exigen-
cies of headline space prevented our stating, more accurately,
"Britain War Office is Piping Down." We regret our having
said "Great Britain" when we should have said "British War
Office." The main trouble is that the representatives of
British jingoism out here are so numerous, so verbose, so
abusive, and so blatant in their claim to represent Great
Britain that there is a tendency at times to take them at their
face value, losing sight for the moment of the splendid work
of their more level-headed and fair-spirited countrymen.
pages.zh:
但是，同样错误的武力政策仍有残留。正是这些东西，是我们彻底且毫不妥协地反对的。我们反对它们，不是因为它们是英国的，而是因为它们与本时代伟大的解放运动步调不一致，而我们正尽力支持这一运动。我们对所谓“挥舞军刀”（saber-rattling）政策的反对，适用于侵略者是英国人、俄罗斯人还是意大利人，无论是美国人、法国人、德国人还是日本人。我们希望中国成为一个自由和主权国家。我们也同样衷心地希望中国永远不会成为对任何其他国家自由的威胁。

我们认为，英国陆军部派遣军队占领上海周边中国领土的计划是最不明智且具挑衅性的，更不用说其中涉及的严重国际法问题了。我们认为，路透社未能发送关于这些计划的任何新闻，尽管这些计划已由一家在伦敦设有通讯员的负责任的美联社发出，这表明有人试图（不一定是路透社上海分社所为）让远东人民对这些计划一无所知。我们认为，散布虚假且误导性报告，称已达成四国协议以保卫上海，是故意的宣传，无论其起源何处。我们相信，军阀和宣传家的这些活动故意迎合了那些当时和现在都试图阻止英国和中国之间和平公正解决的人，并在很大程度上抵消了英国驻华外交官最近以明智、具有政治家风范和公正的态度所创造的良好印象。

几天前情况变得明朗，尽管国内的军国主义者和在华的老牌帝国主义者竭尽全力维持古老的“铁拳”政策，但军队调动正在停止，且不会有更多军队越过香港进行调动。我们在周六向读者发表的议会演讲证实了我们关于这一行动正在进行的结论。随之而来的是最重要的保证，即不会入侵中国领土，军队将留在租界内。此外，情况也已明朗，作为国际治理机构的公共租界工部局董事会并未将租界领土交由英军支配，这些部队必须停留在英国地产上。

我们用简洁的短语表达了对这种沙文主义政策挫败的满意：“大英国正在收敛锋芒（Great Britain is Piping Down）”，这可能并不完全得体。此外，由于标题空间的限制，我们无法更准确地表述为“英国陆军部正在收敛锋芒（Britain War Office is Piping Down）”。我们后悔说了“大英国”，而本应说“英国陆军部”。主要问题在于，此地的英国沙文主义代表人数众多，言辞冗长，充满谩骂，且在声称代表大英国时如此公然，以至于人们有时倾向于按其表面价值看待他们，暂时忽略了他们那些更为头脑冷静和秉持公正精神的同胞所做的出色工作。

pages.en:
One cannot avoid, however, a sense of exultation at the
news of the abandonment of a policy gone into with all the
pomp and pretence of another "War for Civilization." Were
there anything high or noble about the aims of the intended
expedition it might deserve better treatment, but blatant.
boastful and swaggering saber-rattling, partly for its own
sake and partly for the retention of special privileges which
the British Government itself is now definitely pledged to
end, can expect nothing better than scorn when it comes to
an ignominious end. An American view of the situation is
shown in the cartoon which appears on our first page today.

To show our lack of any national bias, we published in
these columns on Saturday last an editorial from a British
newspaper, the "Japan Chronicle" of Kobe. This splendid
publication is one which has always kept to the highest ideals
of Anglo-Saxon journalism in the generation and more of
its existence as a British liberal paper. Incidentally, we
reprint its editorial articles more frequently than does any
other newspaper in Shanghai, and will continue to do so.
Also, when we speak of Britain hereafter, we will try to
remember that the scurrilous campaign of abuse and
dishonesty which we are now witnessing in Shanghai
represents only a part of Britain,—certainly not the
best part. We will also try to remember that for
some of the worst examples of this campaign Britons
are not responsible at all, coming as they do from a paper
the "British" ownership of which is really in the hands of
Asiatic Jews with no understanding whatever of Anglo-
Saxon faith and traditions, and who carry out their part of
the propaganda campaign under a pretence of devotion to
"American ideals."

No, we are not anti-British, in any conceivable national
sense. Any more than we are anti-Chinese, anti-Japanese,
anti-Russian, anti-German, anti-Semite, or anti-American.
We are admittedly anti-Imperialist, anti-privilege, and anti-
humbug. Criticize injustice and wrong we will, regardless
of whose toes we step on. We will try to be fair, and we
make no plea for fairness in return. We are not so naive
as to expect that.
pages.zh:
然而，听到放弃一项伴随着另一场“文明战争”的所有铺张和虚伪的政策的消息，人们不禁感到一种胜利的喜悦。如果预定远征的目标有任何高尚或崇高之处，它或许值得更好的对待，但那种公然的、自夸的和傲慢的“挥舞军刀”，部分是为了其自身目的，部分是为了保留英国政府本身已明确承诺终止的特权，当其以可耻的结局收场时，除了蔑视之外别无所获。今日头版刊登的漫画展示了美国人对局势的看法。

为了表明我们没有任何民族偏见，我们在上周六的本栏刊登了一家英国报纸——神户《日本纪事报》（Japan Chronicle）的社论。这家出色的出版物在其作为一家英国自由派报纸存在的一个多世代里，始终坚守盎格鲁-撒克逊新闻业的最高理想。顺便提一下，我们转载其社论文章的频率高于上海任何其他报纸，并将继续这样做。此外，今后当我们提及英国时，我们将努力记住，我们在上海目睹的这种污蔑性的谩骂和不诚实运动仅代表英国的一部分——肯定不是最好的一部分。我们还将努力记住，对于这场运动中最恶劣的一些例子，英国人根本不负责任，因为这些例子来自一家报纸，其所谓的“英国”所有权实际上掌握在亚洲犹太人手中，他们对盎格鲁-撒克逊的信仰和传统毫无理解，并在伪装忠于“美国理想”的名义下执行其宣传运动的部分任务。

不，我们在任何可想象的民族意义上都不是反英的。就像我们不是反华、反日、反俄、反德、反犹或反美一样。我们承认自己是反帝国主义的、反特权的和反虚伪的。我们将批评不公和错误，不管踩到谁的脚趾。我们将努力保持公正，但我们不乞求回报以公正。我们还没有天真到期待那种回报。

THE CHINA COURIER MONDAY, FEBRUARY 7, 1927.

China's New Year

While most persons were perfectly willing to take a holiday from political worries during the China New Year, the past week was an extraordinarily important one for China, particularly as regards her foreign relations. Most significant of all was the breaking off of the negotiations between the British and Chinese Nationalist governments at Hankow, with a statement from Eugene Chen which resembles closely the proud declaration which has now become one of the great lines of history, amounting, practically, to the statement that the Nationalist Government will not treat with a foreign nation with troops upon Chinese soil.

But there were other things only less significant. First of all, as regards Shanghai, came the news that the British troops en route to Shanghai to occupy Chinese territory surrounding the Settlement would not be permitted by the Municipal Council to use Settlement territory as a base of operations, unless it was on property that was absolutely British owned. Work was halted on the camp which was under construction at Jessfield, and if British troops want to stay here they can do so on British property,—not otherwise.

This, following on the cancellation of the intended saber-rattling demonstration of the S.V.C. the previous Saturday, furnishes final evidence of the thing we pointed out to our reader: a week and a half ago, i.e., that there was no four-power agreement such as was alleged by Reuter's agency for the "defence of Shanghai." This "agreement," now apparently denied by every government which was alleged to have joined Britain in it, was apparently a mere invention of British propagandists who found in the long run that they could not even swing to their purposes the International Settlement in which their control is so predominant, to say nothing of Washington and Tokyo.

On Monday the Foreign Ministry of the Peking Government addressed a note to the British Legation protesting against the despatch of British troops to Shanghai, and asking for the immediate withdrawal of the troops des-patched to China. Britain, it appears, did not deign to reply to this protest. In Hankow, however, there was more definite action, as the Foreign Minister of the Nationalist Government, which had apparently almost reached settlement of many important points in the negotiations with the British Government, broke off the discussions, declaring categorically that the Nationalist Government had never contemplated occupying the International Settlement at Shanghai, that the British military operations here were not only menacing but provocative, and that the concentration of armed British forces at Shanghai, with the information received as to their plans (apparently referring to the British War Office's plan to occupy a big stretch of Chinese territory around Shanghai) "made it impossible.... to view the British concentration.... except as an act of coercion directed against Chinese Nationalism. To sign any agreement in these circumstances would be tantamount to signing under duress or force. The Nationalist Government must perforce await the ending of this period of duress before authorizing the signing of an agreement."

Equally striking is the nature of the memorandum which the British Government presented on its China policy (presented to both the Peking and Hankow Governments). The British concessions Britain is prepared to give up, while they are also willing to waive participation in legal cases of Britishers against Chinese. This latter point does not mean the giving up of extraterritorial rights as regards Britishers, however, the memorandum simply expressing the Government's readiness to consider a revised Chinese penal code for application in British courts in China.

Another point of much interest during the week was the dismissal of Sir Francis Aglen, the British Inspector-General of Customs, by the Peking Government, apparently on account of his refusal to collect the surtaxes where were authorized, and which Peking had requested the Maritime Customs to collect. Britain has protested against this dismissal, but it seems likely to stand.

These things are the big events of the week. They mark the new status which China has attained among the nations of the earth. A year ago Britain would have smiled contemptuously at such an attitude as China's official spokesmen, North and South, are now adopting. There are many "die-hards" who are trying to "laugh it off" today. But the time has passed for this. China has met her old New Year in a new way, a way which means a new life, a new independence, a new order, a new freedom, for the oldest civilization of the world.

《字林西报》 1927年2月7日，星期一。

中国新年

虽然大多数人完全愿意在中国新年期间从政治烦恼中休假，但过去的一周对中国来说极其重要，特别是在外交关系方面。最重要的是英国政府与中国国民政府在汉口的谈判破裂，陈友仁发表了一份声明，该声明与如今已成为历史伟大篇章之一的自豪宣言非常相似，实际上相当于声明国民政府不会与在其领土上驻有军队的外国进行交涉。

但还有其他同样重要的事情。首先，关于上海，传来的消息是，英国军队在前往上海占领租界周围中国领土的途中，除非是在完全属于英国所有的财产上，否则工部局将不允许其使用租界领土作为行动基地。杰斯菲尔德 (Jessfield) 正在建设的营地工程已停止，如果英国军队想留在这里，他们只能留在英国财产上，——别无其他选择。

继上周六取消义勇队 (S.V.C.) 预定的武力示威之后，这为我们向读者指出的事情提供了最终证据：即一周半前，并不存在路透社所称的为了“保卫上海”的四国协议。这个现在显然被所有据称加入英国的政府否认的“协议”，显然只是英国宣传家的发明，他们最终发现，甚至连在他们控制占绝对优势的国际租界都无法为其目的服务，更不用说华盛顿和东京了。

周一，北京政府外交部向英国公使馆发出照会，抗议向上海派遣英国军队，并要求立即撤回派往中国的军队。看来，英国不屑于回复这一抗议。然而，在汉口采取了更明确的行动，国民政府外交部长在与英国政府的谈判中似乎已就许多重要要点达成和解，但他打破了讨论，明确宣布国民政府从未考虑过占领上海国际租界，英国在此的军事行动不仅具有威胁性，而且具有挑衅性，并且英国武装部队在上海的集结，加上收到的有关其计划的情报（显然指的是英国陆军部占领上海周围大片中国领土的计划）“使得……除了将英国的集结……视为针对中国民族主义的胁迫行为外，别无他法。在这种情况下签署任何协议都等同于在胁迫或武力下签字。国民政府必须被迫等待这段胁迫时期结束，才能授权签署协议。”

同样引人注目的是英国政府提出的对华政策备忘录的性质（提交给北京和汉口政府）。英国准备放弃的让步，同时也愿意放弃参与英国人对中国人的法律案件。然而，后一点并不意味着放弃对英国人的治外法权，该备忘录仅表达了政府愿意考虑修订后的中国刑法典，以便在中国的英国法院适用。

本周另一个非常令人关注的点是北京政府解雇了英国海关总税务司安格联爵士 (Sir Francis Aglen)，显然是因为他拒绝征收已获授权且北京要求海关征收的附加税。英国已对此次解雇提出抗议，但似乎维持原判的可能性较大。

这些就是本周的重大事件。它们标志着中国在各国中获得的新地位。一年前，英国会对中国南北官方发言人现在采取的态度报以轻蔑的微笑。今天有许多“顽固派”试图“一笑置之”。但这种时候已经过去了。中国以新的方式迎来了她的旧新年，这种方式意味着这个世界最古老文明的新生活、新独立、新秩序和新自由。

THE CHINA COURIER, TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 8, 1927.

Shanghai, Tuesday, February 8, 1927.

What About Shanghai?

It is interesting to note, in view of some of the sarcastic comments made by various persons of various nationalities regarding America's "inactivity" in connection with the present crisis, and the remarks made about the general nature of America's statement on China policy recently, that the first clear, open, and aboveboard statement regarding Shanghai which has been made by any foreign power had to come from the United States. That this statement, putting forth the definite proposition that Shanghai be declared a neutral zone, is of the greatest importance for all of us here there is no doubt.

The question is, in the main, as to just what is involved. The statement handed out by the American Legation, as reported by Reuter's agency, starts off with an introduction pointing out the huge sums invested in Shanghai, its importance in the trade of the country, and the involving of American interests here, and proposes "that the International Settlement at Shanghai should be excluded from the area of armed conflict so that Americans and other foreigners may receive adequate protection. The American Government," concludes this document, "will be ready on its part to become a party to friendly and orderly negotiations, properly instituted and conducted, regarding the future status of the Settlement."

The representatives of the Chinese Governments have not shown any over-enthusiasm in agreeing to this proposal, which was presented to both the Peking and Nationalist Governments. Chang Tso-lin, according to a report yesterday, preferred to "pass the buck," declaring himself in favor of the proposal, though the matter "belonged entirely to General Sun Chuan-fang and the Southern armies." Another report from Ankuochun headquarters, however, quotes the authorities as stating that the Shanghai district is under their influence, and if they accept it means that the Northern forces alone are to withdraw from this part of the country. "If people really wish to have Shanghai and its vicinity freed from disturbances, Hankow and Kiukiang must also be made buffer zones. We cannot agree to such a proposal as to make Shanghai alone a buffer zone."

The Nationalist Government, it appears, are no more kindly disposed to the proposal. Eugene Chen, however, according to a report received from Peking, made a very pointed response obviously directed towards the drastic measures adopted by the authorities of this part of the country in dealing with the labor movement and the Kuomintang Party, as well as with Chinese Christians who incur their disapproval. Mr. Chen declares that "If General Sun Chuan-fang and the British Municipal authorities of the Shanghai International Settlement had not made such military preparations against the Chinese masses as if they were facing a formidable foe, Shanghai would naturally be freed from the ravages of fighting between the two warring Chinese factions, and the Chinese masses would not be provoked. Therefore, should a disturbance take place at Shanghai, the fault for it entirely lies with the Chinese and British authorities there."

上海，1927年2月8日，星期二。

上海局势如何？

鉴于各界人士针对美国在当前危机中的“不作为”所发表的一些讽刺性评论，以及近期对美国对华政策声明总体性质的议论，值得注意的是，关于上海问题，第一个由外国势力作出的清晰、公开且坦率的声明，竟然来自美国。毫无疑问，该声明提出了将上海宣布为中立区的明确主张，这对我们所有身处此地的人而言至关重要。

问题主要在于，这究竟涉及哪些内容。据路透社报道，美国公使馆发表的声明开篇指出，上海投入了巨额资金，在中国贸易中地位重要，且涉及美国在华利益，并提议“应将上海公共租界排除在武装冲突区域之外，以便美国人及其他外国人获得充分保护。”该文件最后总结道：“美国政府愿意成为一方，参与就租界未来地位所进行的、经适当发起和开展的友好且有序的谈判。”

中国政府代表对这一已向北京政府和国民政府提出的提案，并未表现出过多的热情。据昨日报道，张作霖倾向于“推卸责任”，他宣称自己支持该提案，但此事“完全属于孙传芳将军及南方军队管辖”。然而，另一份来自安国军总部的报告援引当局言论称，上海地区处于其影响之下，如果他们接受该提案，则意味着仅北方军队需从该国这一地区撤出。“如果人们真的希望上海及其周边地区免受动荡之苦，那么汉口和九江也必须被划为缓冲区。我们不能同意仅将上海划为缓冲区的提案。”

看来，国民政府对该提案也未持友善态度。然而，据来自北京的报道，陈友仁作出了非常尖锐的回应，矛头显然指向该地区当局在处理劳工运动、国民党以及那些招致其不满的中国基督徒时所采取的严厉措施。陈先生宣称：“如果孙传芳将军和上海公共租界的英国工部局当局没有像面对强敌那样针对中国民众进行军事准备，上海自然能免于两派中国交战势力之间战火的蹂躏，中国民众也不会受到挑衅。因此，若上海发生动乱，责任完全在于那里的中国和英国当局。”

This bit of logic, however, does not decide the question
practically. Whatever maladministration may have done
towards acerbating relations, here, it would be a terrible
tragedy for a city like Shanghai to be made a scene of war-
fare. In such a warfare not only the foreign interests, and
those of the wealthy Chinese, would suffer. The millions of
the poor herded in their hovels would be the worst suf-
ferers of all if anything like real war approached the city.
The real danger of agreement, and the danger which Mr.
Chen is obviously desirous of avoiding at all times, lies in
the risk of permitting any recognition of the status quo in
Shanghai. The International Settlement is governed by a
body of men utterly unrepresentative of the city,—not even
representative of the foreigners, to say nothing of the
Chinese who make up the bulk of the population and pay the
bulk of the taxes in the city. There have been clashes here
again and again, the May 30th incident of 1925 having
been the most serious and far-reaching in its effects. The
most staid and conservative Chinese, business men with the
widest interests in the Settlement, men who are equally
opposed to civil war and to "Red" influence, are thoroughly
dissatisfied with the manner in which Shanghai is controlled
at the present time.
This is not merely a question of foreign control. While
the wealthiest and most important part of Shanghai lies in
the International and French Concessions, there are other
questions involved. The Chinese sections of the city, separ-
ated as they are by wide stretches of Settlement territory,
present a problem of divided administration which will ap-
parently only be solved when the whole city of Shanghai,
including both the present "foreign" and "Chinese" terri-
tory, is brought under one efficient central administration.
The most practicable administration would appear to be,
at this time, a combined one of foreigners and
Chinese, the Chinese having predominant control. In view
of the extent of foreign interests here, and the big foreign
population, representation of the foreigners in the city ad-
ministration would probably be accepted without demur by
enlightened Chinese officials.
However, the problem presented just now is clear
enough, and complicated enough. How is Shanghai to avoid
the risk of an armed conflict close by, and at the same time
avoid the maintenance of the status quo? If negotiations
were entered into at once in good faith for the changing of
the status of Shanghai, some agreement might be reached
for the maintenance of peace and order here. Will the
Powers rise to the occasion?

然而，这种逻辑并不能在实际层面解决问题。无论管理不善在加剧关系紧张方面起了什么作用，让上海这样的城市沦为战场都将是一场可怕的悲剧。在这样的战争中，不仅外国利益和华人富商的利益会遭受损失。如果真正的战争逼近城市，聚居在简陋棚屋中的数百万贫民将成为受害最深的人群。达成协议的真实危险，也是陈先生显然时刻试图避免的危险，在于承认上海现状的风险。公共租界由一群完全不能代表该市的人治理——甚至不能代表外国人，更不用说占城市人口绝大多数并缴纳大部分税款的中国人了。此处冲突屡见不鲜，其中1925年的五卅惨案后果最为严重且深远。即使是最稳重保守的华人，即在租界拥有广泛利益的商人，那些既反对内战又反对“赤化”影响的人，也对目前控制上海的方式深感不满。

这不仅仅是一个外国控制的问题。虽然上海最富裕和最重要的部分位于公共租界和法租界内，但还涉及其他问题。城市的华人区被大片租界领土分隔开来，造成了行政分裂的问题，这一问题显然只有当整个上海（包括目前的“外国”和“华人”领土）置于一个高效的中枢行政管理之下时，才能得到解决。目前看来，最可行的管理模式是中外联合管理，由中方占据主导控制权。鉴于此处外国利益的规模以及庞大的外籍人口，开明的中国官员可能会毫无异议地接受外国人在城市行政中的代表权。

然而，眼前呈现的问题既清晰又复杂。上海如何在避免附近武装冲突风险的同时，又避免维持现状？如果立即本着诚意就改变上海地位进行谈判，或许能达成某种协议以维持此地的和平与秩序。列强能否把握这一时机？

英国在对华政策上
拥有盟友

法西斯意大利准备
加入英国的武力威慑

（路透社）
罗马，2月6日电。——墨索里尼先生关于中国问题的照会，作为对英国备忘录的回复，是在经过对远东局势的成熟考量并与奥斯汀·张伯伦爵士频繁沟通后，于2月2日发出的。

该照会在次要方面就英意利益不完全一致的某些点保留了意见，但在主要方针上与英国政策保持一致。

据悉，照会中最重要的一部分是声明：如果上海局势变得危急，意大利准备加入英国，甚至使用武力。一封来自罗马的电报声称，据权威消息获悉，一艘意大利无畏舰已前往中国，载有1500名士兵，必要时可作为陆军使用。

（值得注意的是，上述电报注明发自罗马，但其最后一句却称“一封来自罗马的电报声称……”除非罗马人现在将电报作为市内常规的邻里通讯手段，否则其中似乎有些不对劲。了解这封电报的真正来源地将很有趣。也许它和两周前炮制出的四国“保卫上海协定”一样，都出自同样丰富的想象力。编者注）。

THE CHINA COURIER, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 9, 1927.

Britain's Expeditionary Force
An Obituary

The resumption of the negotiations in Hankow between Eugene Chen, Foreign Minister of the Nationalist Government, and Mr. O'Malley, Counsellor of the British Legation, as reported exclusively here in THE CHINA COURIER yesterday morning, is a most significant thing. Just as important as the actual resumption, however, or even more so, are the terms under which the Nationalist Government agreed to meet the British representative again. While these terms are not given with any completeness, it is clear from the Reuter message which appears in another column today that Britain has agreed that the British forces en route to Shanghai are to be disembarked at Hongkong.

In other words, the British War Office is piping down. All the grandiose military display of recent weeks, with the pages upon pages of propaganda spewed forth daily by the British "news" agencies and newspapers, with the high-sounding titles bestowed upon the officers of the "Shanghai Defence Force," with the utterly gratuitous invention by propaganda agencies of an "agreement for the defence of Shanghai," with the deliberate suppression of the actual plans of the British war office and the friendly attitude Washington was taking towards China,—all this gigantic combination of saber-rattling, falsehood, and suppression has dwindled into the movement of a few Indian troops to Shanghai (against the protests of India's national leaders), where they must stay on British territory, keep off the Council's property, and behave themselves.

It has long been clear to the discerning that the swash-buckling Mr. Bull represented by the British propaganda agencies out here was not really the master of the situation. The statements made by official spokesmen of the British government, such as Austen Chamberlain and the accredited diplomatic representatives, trying to meet China's demands half-way, were too widely at variance with the cheap bluff of the militarists to admit of much compromise. It was not impossible, of course, that Britain was playing a double game: Britain is not the only Government to have done so. Nevertheless, the necessity of subterfuge and double-dealing to the extent attempted is certainly no evidence of strength.

From the beginning the policy of deception was followed. First Reuter's sent through a telegram reporting an agreement among Britain, Japan, France and America "for the defence of Shanghai" in a military sense. This report was apparently a pure invention of Reuter's, and had no existence in fact. The British war office plans, as reported by "United Press" in a special dispatch from London, included the seizure of points outside Shanghai, in other words, the invasion of Chinese territory. This apparently accurate report Reuter did not see fit to advise us of.

Governments, however, are pretty well informed these days, even though private citizens may be victimized and misled by propaganda organs of various kinds. 英国远征军
讣告

正如本报昨晨独家报道的那样，国民政府外交部长陈友仁与英国公使馆参赞欧马利先生之间在汉口的谈判得以恢复，这是一件极具意义的事情。然而，与谈判实际恢复同等重要、甚至更为重要的是，国民政府同意再次会见英国代表的条件。虽然这些条件并未完整公布，但从今天另一栏刊登的路透社消息中可以清楚看出，英国已同意将在途前往上海的英国部队在香港卸船登陆。

换言之，英国陆军部正在收敛声势。近几周来所有宏大的军事展示，包括英国“新闻”机构和报纸每日连篇累牍喷涌出的宣传，授予“上海防卫队”军官的那些冠冕堂皇的头衔，宣传机构凭空捏造的所谓“保卫上海协定”，以及对英国陆军部实际计划和华盛顿对华友好态度的刻意压制——所有这一切由武力威慑、谎言和压制组成的巨大组合，已萎缩为少数印度部队调往上海的行动（此举违背了印度民族领袖的抗议），而这些部队必须留在英国领土上，不得踏入工部局地产，并须循规蹈矩。

敏锐的观察家早已清楚，英国宣传机构在此地所描绘的那位好斗的“约翰牛”先生并非局势的真正主宰者。英国政府官方发言人（如奥斯汀·张伯伦）及 accredited 外交代表所作的声明，试图在一定程度上满足中国的要求，这与军方廉价的虚张声势大相径庭，难以妥协。当然，英国玩弄两面手法并非不可能：英国并非唯一这样做的政府。尽管如此，试图如此程度地进行诡辩和两面派行事，绝非实力的证明。

从一开始，欺骗政策便一直奉行。首先，路透社通过电报发布消息称，英国、日本、法国和美国达成了军事意义上“保卫上海”的协定。该报道显然是路透社的纯粹杜撰，事实上并不存在。据“合众社”从伦敦发出的特别专电报道，英国陆军部的计划包括占领上海以外的据点，换句话说，即入侵中国领土。对于这一看似准确的报道，路透社认为不宜告知我们。

然而，如今的各国政府消息相当灵通，尽管平民百姓可能会成为各种宣传机构的受害者和被误导者。中国当局显然对英国军方入侵中国领土的计划毫不怀疑，在北京提出抗议之后，随之而来的是

definite breaking off of negotiations by the Nationalist Gov-
ernment at Hankow, which stated in no uncertain terms
that it could not treat with Britain while British forces were
being concentrated in Shanghai as a "Chinese Expeditionary
Force."
This was reported on February 1st. On February 2d
and 3d the "United Press," the big American news agency,
sent out the following reports, which we are unable to find
that Reuter's agency ever informed us of:
London, Feb. 2.—It is authoritatively learned
that Sir Austen Chamberlain, Secretary for Foreign
Affairs, is claiming that force will be used in China
only as a last resort in the event of onslaughts by
uncontrolled mobs.
A statement to this effect will be given out
soon, it is understood.
This basis, it is thought, permits Eugene Chen
and Mr. O'Malley to reach an agreement immediate-
ly in their Hankow negotiations so far as Shanghai
is concerned.
It will allow not only a suspension of the British
preparations for defense at Shanghai, but will halt
the sending of reinforcements which are now at
Hongkong en route to Shanghai.
London, Feb. 3.—The Cabinet is drafting in-
structions, it was learned today, on a basis of which
Mr. O'Malley, British special representative in Han-
kow, may negotiate a basis for settlement with
Eugene Chen, Nationalist Minister for Foreign
Affairs.
It is understood that if Chen is able to furnish
satisfactory guarantee as to the safety of British
lives and property at Shanghai, British forces now
en route to Shanghai will be diverted to Hongkong.
That something of this kind was going on was evident
from various things. First of all came the stoppage of
work on the camp being prepared for the troops at Jessfield.
Then came the news that Hongkong was making prepara-
tions for the billeting of large numbers of troops. The
Reuter messages of the gigantic forces moving on to Shang-
hai dwindled both in bulk and enthusiasm. Finally, though
Reuter had carried no messages as to the decisions made
at London tying the hands of the swashbucklers, there came
the resumption of the negotiations at Hankow, which could
only mean that the British War Office had piped down. And
then, in a most ambiguous sentence which appears to refer
to Britain as the proposer, they mention "the proposal that
the British forces now en route to Shanghai should be dis-
embarked at Hongkong" as having been favorably commented
on by the (Nationalist) officials.
So this appears to be the sad end of the China Ex-
peditionary Force, the "four-power agreement for the de-
fence of Shanghai," the 20,000 bold bad Britishers who were
coming to occupy Chinese territory in this vicinity, and the
noble line of grandiose titles which headed the "Shanghai
Defence Force." But we can't weep for the dead,—parti-
cularly when it happened to be only a miscarriage.

汉口国民政府明确中断谈判，毫不含糊地表示，只要英军以“中国远征军”的名义集结于上海，便无法与英国进行交涉。
此事于2月1日报导。2月2日和3日，美国大型新闻机构“合众社”（United Press）发布了以下报导，而我们发现路透社从未向我们通报过这些消息：
伦敦，2月2日。——据权威消息获悉，外交大臣奥斯汀·张伯伦爵士（Sir Austen Chamberlain）声称，只有在遭受失控暴民攻击的情况下，才会将使用武力作为最后手段。
据悉，一份以此为宗旨的声明即将发布。
人们认为，这一基础使得尤金·陈（Eugene Chen）和欧马利先生（Mr. O'Malley）在汉口谈判中能够就上海问题立即达成协议。
这不仅将使英国在上海的防御准备工作暂停，还将停止目前正在从香港前往上海的增援部队的派遣。
伦敦，2月3日。——据悉，内阁今日正在起草指示，英国驻汉口特别代表欧马利先生可据此与国民党外交部长尤金·陈协商解决方案的基础。
据了解，如果陈能提供令人满意的保证，确保上海英国人生命财产的安全，目前正前往上海的英军将改道前往香港。
从各种迹象来看，显然正在发生此类事情。首先，为部队在兆丰公园（Jessfield）准备的营地工程停工。接着传来消息，香港正在为大量部队的驻扎做准备。路透社关于庞大军队开赴上海的报导，无论在篇幅还是热情上都大幅缩减。最后，虽然路透社没有发布任何关于伦敦做出束缚那些好战分子手脚的决定之消息，但汉口恢复了谈判，这只能意味着英国陆军部已经退缩。随后，在一句似乎指英国为提议方的模棱两可的句子中，他们提到“将目前正前往上海的英军在香港登陆”的提议已得到（国民党）官员的正面评价。
因此，这似乎是“中国远征军”、“四国保卫上海协定”、即将来此占领中国领土的两万名凶恶英国人，以及领衔“上海防卫队”的那一连串宏伟头衔的悲惨结局。但我们无需为死者哀悼，——尤其是当这仅仅是一次流产的时候。

Mr. Francis Zia, Managing
Editor of THE CHINA COURIER and
of the "China Tribune," was kid-
napped at the corner of Hankow
and Shantung Roads, a block from
the Central Police Station, Satur-
day afternoon at 5.45, and is now a
prisoner at the yamen of Gen. Li
Pao-chang, Defence Commissioner
of Shanghai and Woosung. Mr.
Zia is charged with having cir-
culated reports through The China
Courier, referring to reverses to
Sun Chuan-fang's forces in Che-
kiang, which were dangerous to the
public mind. Gen. Li, in a state-
ment yesterday, declared that he
was responsible for the mainten-
ance of peace and good order in
this district, and it was for the
maintenance of peace and good
order that Mr. Zia was kidnapped
by his armed agents in the Inter-
national Settlement and taken to
the yamen where he is now detain-
ed. Gen. Li declared to inter-
viewers yesterday that the kid-
napping was done with the full
knowledge of the Commissioner of
Police, though Major Johnson denied this last night.

Visit Office
Two husky individuals came to
the office of THE CHINA COURIER
on Saturday afternoon and asked
to see Mr. Zia. Upon being ad-
mitted to his office they declared
they much resented certain reports
which had appeared in the paper
regarding a defeat for Sun Chuang-
fang's forces, and asked Mr. Zia
to come with them to the Bureau
for Foreign Affairs. The invita-
tion was declined, but Mr. Zia told
the men that if there was any re-
port in the paper which was in-
accurate he would be quite willing
to print a correction, if they would
write one out for him. This did
not suit the visitors, who after con-
siderable argument left the office.
Soon after this Mr. Zia went to
the office of the "Shun Pao," the
big Chinese newspaper, on busi-
ness. While in this office, which
is on the southwest corner of Han-
kow and Shantung Roads, a motor
car drew up on Shantung Road
opposite the entrance of the "Shun
Pao," across the street from where
the private ricsha was awaiting
Mr. Zia. When the journalist left
the building and walked to his
ricsha three men from the car
crossed the street to him. One
seized him by the arm on each side,
and one stood behind him, at the
same time pressing revolvers to his
ribs, one of them saying "Now I
suppose you will come along with
us." Mr. Zia tried to resist, and
the ricsha coolie, who had hold of
his hand, tried to pull him away
from the men, but the frail little
journalist was no match for three
opponents, who hurried him across
the street and into the waiting
motor-car, which started swiftly
out Shantung Road and was soon
lost to view.

Kidnappers Discovered
The description of two of the
men who did the kidnapping tallies
with that of the men who visited
the office of THE CHINA COURIER
earlier in the day, and they
were probably the same parties.
After Mr. Zia's disappearance the
ricsha coolie hurried back to THE
CHINA COURIER and told what
had happened, and efforts were
immediately made to trace the vic-
tims. At first it was thought that
the motive was robbery, as Mr. Zia
had several hundred dollars on his
person at the time, but when in-
vestigation showed that the car
number, 8673, belonged to a Mr.
Liu who is closely connected with
the Merchant Volunteers, it was
suspected that the motive was poli-
tical.
About eight o'clock this belief
was confirmed by a telephone mes-
sage from the Defence Commis-
sioner's yamen, stating that Mr. Zia
was being held in custody for print-
ing false reports in THE CHINA
COURIER and that he would be
tried by a military court on Sun-
day. A little later a well-known
American journalist here visited
Mr. Hau Yuan, Acting Mayor of
Shanghai and Commissioner of
Foreign Affairs, in an effort to
secure Mr. Zia's liberation, but was
unsuccessful.

Delegation to Yamen
On Sunday afternoon a repre-
sentative of THE CHINA COURIER,
in company with a delega-
tion including four of the most pro-
minent American and British jour-
nalists in Shanghai, visited Gen.
Li Pao-chang at the yamen, and
inquired as to the charges against
Mr. Zia. It was pointed out to
the General that a kidnapping of
this kind was likely to create a very
bad impression among foreigners
both here and in America and Eng-
land. In addition to four local
publications, there were three of
the biggest of American dailies re-
presented in the delegation, and
British daily, papers with an ag-
gregate circulation of many mil-
lions.
Gen. Li, speaking through an
interpreter, explained that a cer-
tain article had appeared in The
China Courier reporting a reverse
for Sun Chuan-fang's forces in
Chekiang. He considered this arti-
cle dangerous to the public peace,
and as he was entrusted with the
maintenance of peace and good
order in this district Mr. Zia was
now being detained.

A Reuter Report
It was pointed out by Mr. How-
ard, Associate Editor of The
China Courier, that the article re-
porting the reverse of Sun's forces
was received through Reuter's a
British news agency, and was also
published in other foreign news-
papers in Shanghai. Furthermore,
Mr. Howard explained, he was per-
sonally responsible for the article
having been inserted in the paper,
as in his work as Associate Editor
he received news reports of this
kind from various agencies and saw
to their publication. Mr. Zia knew
nothing whatever of the reports in
question until he saw them in print
the next day.
Gen. Li made no reply to the
statement that the report in ques-
tion emanated from Reuter's
agency, contenting himself with a
response that Mr. Zia, as Managing
Editor, was responsible for what
appeared in the paper. The reports
were dangerous to peace and order,
and General was entrusted with the
preservation of peace and good
order here.
We give on Page 2 today the two
articles which are said to be dan-
gerous to the public peace.

Prominent Catholic
Mr. Zia is a native of Kwantung
Province, and is a prominent Ca-
tholic. In his youth he was
educated at the St. Francis Xavier
School. He had in the course of
his business career developed a
great liking for journalism, and
had contributed voluminously to
the columns of newspapers wher-
ever he happened to be. While in
Weihaiwei some twenty years ago
he started the "Republican Oriental
Messenger," and this was followed
by a number of other journals in
the English language under his
editorship.
The path of a journalist is how-
ever not always strewn with roses,
and as a consequence most of his
early attempts are now mere past
history. At one time he was the
English secretary of the Chinese
General Chamber of Commerce in
Shanghai, and in this capacity he
has rendered significant services in
bringing the Chinese viewpoint in
matters of public interest to the
foreign community. A reference to
the correspondence columns of
Shanghai papers of those days will
show that his views are always
sane and moderate, and far from
being dangerously radical.
In addition to his journalistic
activities, Mr. Zia has been an
official of the Young Men's Chris-
tian Association, and is connected
with the Boy Scouts and several
Sino-foreign associations.
In March last year Mr. Zia start-
ed the "China Tribune," a bi-lin-
gual weekly, and in July, in asso-
ciation with some local Americans
and Chinese, he started THE CHINA
COURIER, of which he has been
Director and Manager Editor.

《中国信使报》（THE CHINA COURIER）及《中国论坛报》（China Tribune）总编辑谢福松（Francis Zia）先生，于周六下午5时45分在汉口路与山东路转角处、距中央巡捕房一个街区的地方被绑架，目前被囚禁于上海及吴淞防卫督办李宝章将军的衙门内。谢先生被指控通过《中国信使报》散布有关孙传芳部队在浙江失利的消息，认为这些消息危害公众心理。李将军昨日发表声明称，他负责维持本地区的和平与秩序，正是为了维护和平与秩序，谢先生才由其武装人员在公共租界内被绑架并带至衙门，现正被拘押于此。李将军昨日对记者宣称，此次绑架行动是在警务处处长的完全知情下进行的，尽管约翰逊少校昨晚对此予以否认。

走访办公室
周六下午，两名体格魁梧的人来到《中国信使报》办公室，要求见谢先生。获准进入其办公室后，他们表示对该报刊登的关于孙传芳部队战败的某些报道深感不满，并要求谢先生随他们前往交涉署。谢先生拒绝了这一“邀请”，但他告诉这些人，如果报上有任何不实的报道，只要他们写出更正稿，他很乐意刊登更正。来访者对此并不满意，经过一番争论后离开了办公室。

此后不久，谢先生因公务前往大型中文报纸《申报》的办公室。当谢先生身处位于汉口路与山东路西南角的《申报》办公室时，一辆汽车停在山东路上，正对《申报》入口，隔着街道，谢先生的私人黄包车正在那里等候。当这位记者走出大楼走向他的黄包车时，车上的三名男子穿过街道向他走来。其中两人分别抓住他的一只手臂，另一人站在他身后，同时用左轮手枪顶住他的肋部，其中一人说道：“我想你现在会跟我们走了。”谢先生试图反抗，抓着他手的黄包车夫也试图将他从那些人手中拉开，但这位瘦弱的记者无法抵挡三名对手，他们迅速将他拖过街道，推进等候的汽车中。汽车随即沿山东路快速驶离，很快消失在视线中。

绑匪身份查明
实施绑架的两名男子的体貌特征与当天早些时候造访《中国信使报》办公室的男子相符，他们很可能就是同一伙人。谢先生失踪后，黄包车夫急忙返回《中国信使报》告知所发生的情况，人们立即着手寻找受害者。起初人们认为动机是抢劫，因为谢先生当时身上带着数百美元，但当调查显示车牌号为8673的汽车属于一位与商团义勇队关系密切的刘姓先生时，人们怀疑动机是政治性的。

大约八点钟，这一猜测得到了来自防卫督办衙门的电话证实，电话称谢先生因在《中国信使报》刊登虚假报道而被拘留，并将于周日接受军事法庭审判。稍后，一位在此地的知名美国记者拜访了上海代市长兼交涉员侯源（Hau Yuan，音译）先生，试图争取释放谢先生，但未获成功。

代表团前往衙门
周日下午，《中国信使报》的一名代表与一个代表团一同前往李宝章将军的衙门，该代表团包括四位上海最杰出的英美记者，并就针对谢先生的指控进行质询。代表团向将军指出，此类绑架行为很可能在上海以及在美国和英国的外国人中造成极坏的印象。除了四家本地出版物外，代表团中还代表了三家发行量最大的美国日报以及一家英国日报，这些报纸的总发行量达数百万份。

李将军通过翻译解释说，《中国信使报》刊登了一篇文章，报道了孙传芳部队在浙江的失利。他认为这篇文章危害公共和平，鉴于他受委托维持本地区的和平与良好秩序，因此谢先生目前被拘留。

路透社报道
《中国信使报》副主编霍华德（Howard）先生指出，报道孙军失利的文章是通过英国新闻机构路透社收到的，并且也刊登在上海的其他外文报纸上。此外，霍华德先生解释说，他个人对该文章被刊登在报纸上负责，因为作为副主编，他的工作是从各个机构接收此类新闻报道并安排发表。谢先生直到第二天看到印刷版之前，对这些报道一无所知。

对于有关报道源自路透社的说法，李将军未作回应，仅回答说谢先生作为总编辑，应对报纸上刊登的内容负责。这些报道危害和平与秩序，而将军受命在此地维护和平与良好秩序。

我们今天在第2版刊登了两篇据称危害公共和平的文章。

知名天主教徒
谢先生是广东省人，也是一位知名的天主教徒。他年轻时曾在圣方济各沙勿略学校（St. Francis Xavier School）受教育。在他的职业生涯中，他对新闻业产生了浓厚的兴趣，并在其所到之处为多家报纸的专栏大量撰稿。大约二十年前他在威海卫期间，创办了《共和东方信使报》（Republican Oriental Messenger），随后又在他主编下创办了其他数种英文期刊。

然而，记者的道路并非总是铺满玫瑰，因此他早期的多数尝试如今已成为历史。他曾一度担任上海华人总商会的英文秘书，在此职位上，他在向外国社群传达华人在公共利益事务上的观点方面做出了重要贡献。查阅当时上海报纸的读者来信专栏可以看出，他的观点始终理智且温和，绝非危险的激进分子。

除了新闻活动外，谢先生还曾担任基督教青年会（YMCA）的官员，并与童子军及数个中外协会有关联。去年三月，谢先生创办了双语周刊《中国论坛报》，七月，他与一些当地美国人和中国人合作，创办了《中国信使报》，他一直担任该报的董事兼总经理兼总编辑。

MR. FRANCIS ZIA
UNDER ARREST

Carried Off from the Settlement
to Lunghua Yamen on Satur-
day Evening

CHARGE OF SEDITIOUS
PUBLICATION

Another daring kidnapping case
occurred on Saturday afternoon in
the heart of the central district, the
victim being Mr. Francis Zia, a
well-known Chinese resident, whose
activities in certain directions have
brought him prominently before the
notice of foreigners and who is now
managing editor of the "China
Courier" and the "China Tribune".

It appears that Mr. Zia left the
offices of the "Shunpao," the well-
known Chinese newspaper, situated
at the corner of Hankow and Shan-
tung Roads, and was walking to his
private ricksha a few paces from
the entrance to the building, when
three armed men presented their

Mr. Zia's Activities

Mr. Zia, whose full name is Zia
Foh-sung, is a native of Kuangtung
and a graduate of St. Francis
Xavier's College. Adhering to the
Roman Catholic Church, he is also
a member of the Chinese Y.M.C.A.
and very active in connexion with
its work. After teaching in the
Anglo-Chinese College in Tientsin,
he served in different capacities, for
some time being under Sir James
Stewart Lockhart, Administrator
of the Territory of Weihaiwei. He
then came to Shanghai and worked
with the now defunct "Shanghai
Gazette" as translator, at the same
time being a member of the editorial
staff of the "Shunpao". He was at
one time English secretary to the
Chinese General Chamber of Com-
merce also editing a small
paper for Chinese students of Eng-
lish, known as "Francis Zia's
Weekly." Mr. Zia possesses great
versatility in languages, and can
read and write French, German and
Spanish, and some Japanese besides
English and Chinese. He is connected
with many Sino-foreign organiza-
tions, is an officer of the Sino-
Japanese Society, and English
secretary to the Shanghai Chinese
Newspapermen's Association and
the Shanghai Press Club.

It is definitely known that Mr.
Zia is being detained at the military
headquarters at Lunghua and that
the car which took him there was one
belonging to Gen. Li Pao-chang,
Commissioner of Defence for the

Shanghai and Woosung Districts.

At first it was thought that Mr.
Zia had been kidnapped for ransom
and for a large sum of money which
he was carrying to pay his staff
before the China New Year, but
this is incorrect, as it is definitely
known that he was taken to the
Lunghua Yamen, though no official
charge had been preferred against
him. It is believed that the military
authorities took action because of
certain articles which appeared in
Mr. Zia's papers relating to the
military situation. These were said
to be of a seditious nature and in
support of the Kuomintang expedi-
tion against Marshal Sun Chuan-
fang, who recently issued an order
forbidding Chinese papers to publish
any comments on the war situation.

MR. FRANCIS ZIA

pistols at him and ordered him to
keep quiet and follow them. Mr.
Zia was then pushed into a motor
car, No. 8673, which was waiting
near by, and driven off.

《字林西报》，1927年1月31日，星期一

谢福松先生
被捕

周六晚间从租界被带至龙华衙门

指控刊登煽动性出版物

周六下午，在中心区域的核心地带发生了另一起大胆的绑架案，受害者是知名华人居民谢福松（Francis Zia）先生，他在某些方面的活动使其显著地受到外国人的关注，他目前是《中国信使报》和《中国论坛报》的总编辑。

据悉，谢先生离开位于汉口路与山东路转角的知名中文报纸《申报》办公室，正走向离大楼入口几步远处的私人黄包车时，三名持枪男子向他出示了

谢先生的活动

谢先生，全名谢福松（Zia Foh-sung），广东人，毕业于圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College）。他信奉罗马天主教，也是中华基督教青年会会员，并积极从事相关工作。在天津中英学院任教后，他担任过各种职务，有一段时间在威海卫行政长官司徒尔特·洛克哈特爵士（Sir James Stewart Lockhart）手下任职。随后他来到上海，在现已停刊的《上海公报》（Shanghai Gazette）担任翻译，同时又是《申报》编辑部的成员。他曾一度担任华人总商会的英文秘书，还编辑了一份供中国学生学习英语的小报，名为《谢福松周报》（Francis Zia's Weekly）。谢先生具备极强的语言天赋，除英语和中文外，还能读写法语、德语和西班牙语，并懂一些日语。他与许多中外组织有关联，是中日协会的职员，也是上海华人新闻记者协会和上海记者俱乐部的英文秘书。

可以确定的是，谢先生被关押在龙华的军事总部，带他去那里的汽车属于上海及吴淞地区防卫督办李宝章将军。

起初人们以为谢先生是为了赎金以及他携带的一笔用于在春节前支付员工薪水的大额现金而被绑架，但这并不正确，因为已确切得知他被带往龙华衙门，尽管当时并未对他提出正式指控。据信，军方采取行动是因为谢先生报纸上刊登的某些有关军事局势的文章。这些文章据称具有煽动性质，并支持国民党反对孙传芳元帅的远征，孙传芳最近发布命令，禁止中文报纸发表任何关于战争局势的评论。

谢福松先生

手枪并命令他保持安静并跟随他们。谢先生随后被推入附近等候的一辆编号为8673的汽车，并被驾车带走。

------------

.............另从同一消息来源获悉，“The China Courier”（《中国信使报》），Kentwell 在该报持有大量股份，今后将被用作国民党的官方外文机关报，以宣传其主义..............
